channel.title: The Sukhi Play blog
channel.description: Announcements, guides for parents of small children, and what happened behind the scenes, by Mandeep Singh.

item.title: Sukhi's Railway: a train set on the screen, and my first experiment
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: A free track-building toy for ages three to five. It is an experiment: on the website only, not in Sukhi Play, until I know children love it.

item.title: Parental controls or a locked-down browser for an under-five?
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Parental controls filter what an older child finds online. An under-five needs containment: one screen, only the sites you chose, and no way out.

item.title: Printable name labels, stickers and bookmarks for children
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Jazz's Studio is a free stationery maker for children of seven and up: name labels, stickers, bookmarks, gift tags and door signs, each on one A4 page.

item.title: Screen time for a three-year-old: the guidance and what works
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: The WHO says no more than an hour of sedentary screen time a day for ages two to four, and less is better. Short sessions and a calm stop make it workable.

item.title: How I set up Sukhi Play for my three-year-old
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Start with two or three tiles, sit beside them for the first sessions, set a short play time and add sites slowly. The setup I would repeat, step by step.

item.title: Why toddlers bash the keyboard, and a safe place to let them
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Toddlers bash keys because every press does something and they copy you. On a normal computer that hits shortcuts; a locked-down screen makes it safe.

item.title: How to let a toddler use your laptop without losing your work
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Give them a space your work is not in: their own user account, a locked-down browser with only the sites you chose, and your work saved and closed first.

item.title: Jazz's Studio: stationery to design and print, for ages 7 and up
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Jazz's Studio, new in Sukhi Play 2.2 and grown up in 2.3, lets children of seven and up design and print their own stickers, labels, diaries and more.

item.title: Why Sukhi Play moved from MIT to a personal-use licence
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: From 2.1, Sukhi Play is free for families to use, change and share, but never for commercial use or organisations. 2.0.2 and earlier stay under MIT.

item.title: Sukhi Colouring: the first app made for Sukhi Play
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Sukhi Colouring is a free colouring book for small children, made for Sukhi Play and also running in any browser, offline, with no account and no adverts.

item.title: What went wrong with Sukhi Play 2.0, and why it's missing from the release page
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Look for 2.0.0 on the releases page and it isn't there. Here's why, and the two other things that went wrong around the same release.

item.title: Play time limits: a session that ends on its own
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Sukhi Play can now end a session by itself: set a length once, your child sees no countdown until the last thirty seconds, then a stop screen.

item.title: Sukhi Play 2.0: a catalogue, and apps that work offline
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Sukhi Play 2.0 adds a one-tap catalogue of sites, three apps inside the download that work with no internet, and a rebuilt grown-up screen.

item.title: Sukhi Play 1.0, a locked-down browser for small children
item.dc:creator: Mandeep Singh
item.description: Sukhi Play 1.0 is a free kiosk browser for macOS, Windows and Linux that shows a small child only the websites a grown-up chose, and nothing else.
